     Add projectId to task forms; fix AI suggestion failing on null dueDate

     Context

     Two issues found after building the UI:
     1. UI_DESIGN.md's field lists didn't mention projectId, but leaving it out
        of the create/update forms means the update form silently clears a
        task's project on every save (full-replace PUT) and there's no way to
        associate a task with a project via the UI at all. The user now wants it
        added to both forms.
     2. AiTaskSuggestion's prompt legitimately allows the model to return
        dueDate: null when the user's query has no natural deadline (e.g. "buy
        milk") — but TaskRequestDto.dueDate is @NotNull, so parseAndValidate
        throws AiSuggestionException (and burns all 3 retries) on every one of
        those otherwise-perfectly-valid responses. The user asked to fix this
        either by forcing the LLM to always supply a date, or by defaulting it
        ourselves — defaulting ourselves is the more robust choice (doesn't
        depend on LLM instruction-following fidelity across all 3 retry
        attempts) and mirrors the exact pattern already used for status (AI
        doesn't decide it, the backend forces a sensible value post-parse).

     Approach

     service/AiService.java — in parseAndValidate, right after the JSON parses
     successfully but before running Bean Validation (unlike status, dueDate is
     @NotNull/@FutureOrPresent-constrained, so the default must land before
     validation runs, not after): if suggestion.getDueDate() == null, set it to
     LocalDate.now().plusDays(7) — a one-week-out default, applied the same way
     regardless of why it's missing. No prompt changes needed — the prompt's "or
     null" rule stays accurate, the backend now just handles that case
     gracefully instead of failing on it.

     src/test/java/com/eulerity/taskmanager/service/AiServiceTest.java — add
     suggestTask_missingDueDate_appliesDefaultDueDate(): same mocked safety
     pass, but the suggestion response JSON omits dueDate (or sends null);
     assert the returned TaskRequestDto.getDueDate() equals
     LocalDate.now().plusDays(7), and that it doesn't throw.

     src/main/resources/static/index.html:
     - Add a <select id="ct-projectId"> to the create-task form and a <select 
       id="ut-projectId"> to the update-task form, both with a default "None"
       (value="") option plus one <option> per project (value=project.id,
       text=project.name).
     - New populateProjectDropdowns(projects) function that rebuilds both
       selects' options; called at the end of renderProjects(...) so the
       dropdowns stay in sync every time the project list is fetched or
       refreshed (including after a project delete).
     - Call fetchProjects() once on page load (DOMContentLoaded) so the
       dropdowns have data immediately, not only after the user manually clicks
       "Get Projects."
     - createTask(): include projectId: value ? Number(value) : null in the
       request body; reset ct-projectId to "" on successful create, same as the
       other fields.
     - startTaskUpdate(id): set ut-projectId.value to task.project ? 
       String(task.project.id) : '' when populating the form.
     - submitTaskUpdate(): include projectId in the PUT body the same way
       createTask does. This also resolves the earlier caveat (updating a task
       used to always clear its project since projectId was never sent) — it's
       now preserved/changeable via the dropdown.

     Files changed

     - service/AiService.java — default dueDate before validation
     - src/test/java/com/eulerity/taskmanager/service/AiServiceTest.java — one

     once already, right at its start (the transcript.md scrape's first lines

        16 +> ## Context                                                 
        17 +> The project is a freshly generated Spring Boot 4.1.1 app (J
           +ava 17, Maven) with only `TaskmanagerApplication` present und
           +er `com.eulerity.taskmanager`. Dependencies already include S
           +pring Web MVC, Spring Data JPA, Bean Validation, and H2. The 
           +user wants to build this incrementally, guided step by step, 
           +starting with the standard layered package layout before any 
           +real functionality is added:                                 
        18 +>                                                            
        19 +> - `controller/` — REST API entry points                    
        20 +> - `service/` — business logic                              
        21 +> - `dto/` — request/response API contract objects           
        22 +> - `entity/` — JPA/DB model entities                        
        23 +> - `repository/` — Spring Data repository layer             
        24 +>                                                            
        25 +> ## Approach                                                
        26 +> Create the five packages under `src/main/java/com/eulerity/
           +taskmanager/`:                                               
        27 +>

        29 +> src/main/java/com/eulerity/taskmanager/                    
        30 +> ├── TaskmanagerApplication.java   (existing, unchanged)    
        31 +> ├── controller/                                            
        32 +> ├── service/                                               
        33 +> ├── dto/                                                   
        34 +> ├── entity/                                                
        35 +> └── repository/                                            
        36 +> ```                                                        
        37 +>                                                            
        38 +> Since git does not track empty directories, each new packag
           +e will get a minimal `package-info.java` (standard Java conve
           +ntion) so the folder exists, is committed, and shows up corre
           +ctly in IDEs — rather than an off-convention `.gitkeep` file.
           + These `package-info.java` files contain no logic, just the `
           +package` declaration.                                        
        39 +>                                                            
        40 +> No changes to `pom.xml` (dependencies already cover web/JPA

       282 +> # Add Project and Task JPA entities                        
       283 +>                                                            
       284 +> ## Context                                                 
       285 +> The project has an empty `entity/` package and the standard
           + JPA/H2/validation dependencies already in `pom.xml`. The use
           +r wants to define the core domain model — `Project` and `Task
           +` — as JPA entities, so future steps (repository, service, DT
           +O, controller wiring) can build real logic on top of them ins
           +tead of the current dummy stubs.                             
       286 +>                                                            
       287 +> **Note on the enum package:** the user asked for the priori
           +ty/status enums to live in a package literally called `enum` 
           +inside `entity`. `enum` is a reserved keyword in Java and can
           +not be used as a package name — the project would fail to com
           +pile. This plan uses `entity.enums` (plural) instead, which i
           +s the standard workaround. Flagging this here for visibility 
           +— let me know if you'd prefer a different name (e.g. `entity.
           +type`).                                                      
       288 +>                                                            
       289 +> ## Approach                                                
       290 +>                                                            
       291 +> ### Enums — `entity/enums/`                                
       292 +> - `TaskPriority.java` — `LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH`                
       293 +> - `TaskStatus.java` — `TODO, IN_PROGRESS, DONE`            
       294 +>                                                            
       295 +> ### `entity/Project.java`                                  
       296 +> - `@Entity @Table(name = "project")`                       
       297 +> - `id`: `Long`, `@Id @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationT
           +ype.IDENTITY)`                                               
       298 +> - `name`: `String`, `@Column(nullable = false)` (required) 
       299 +> - `description`: `String`, plain `@Column` (nullable/option
           +al by default)                                               
       300 +> - `tasks`: `List<Task>`, `@OneToMany(mappedBy = "project", 
           +fetch = FetchType.LAZY)` — lazy-loaded, no cascade, initializ
           +ed to an empty `ArrayList` so it's never null, just possibly 
           +empty                                                        
       301 +> - No-arg constructor plus plain getters/setters — no Lombok
           + in this project                                             
       302 +>                                                            
       303 +> ### `entity/Task.java`                                     
       304 +> - `@Entity @Table(name = "task")`                          
       305 +> - `id`: `Long`, `@Id @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationT
           +ype.IDENTITY)`                                               
       306 +> - `title`: `String`, `@Column(nullable = false)` (required)
       307 +> - `description`: `String`, plain `@Column` (optional)      
       308 +> - `dueDate`: `LocalDate`, maps to `due_date` column (Hibern
           +ate's default naming strategy converts camelCase → snake_case
           + automatically)                                              
       309 +> - `priority`: `TaskPriority`, `@Enumerated(EnumType.STRING)
           +`                                                            
       310 +> - `status`: `TaskStatus`, `@Enumerated(EnumType.STRING)`   
       311 +> - `project`: `Project`, `@ManyToOne(fetch = FetchType.LAZY)
           + @JoinColumn(name = "project_id", nullable = true)` — a task 
           +belongs to at most one project, and it's optional            
       312 +> - Plain getters/setters, no-arg constructor                
       313 +>                                                            
       314 +> No changes needed to `pom.xml` or `application.properties` 
           +— Spring Boot auto-configures an embedded H2 datasource with 
           +`ddl-auto=create-drop` by default when no datasource is expli
           +citly configured.                                            
       315 +>                                                            
       316 +> ## Files to create                                         
       317 +> - `src/main/java/com/eulerity/taskmanager/entity/enums/Task
           +Priority.java`                                               
       318 +> - `src/main/java/com/eulerity/taskmanager/entity/enums/Task
           +Status.java`                                                 
       319 +> - `src/main/java/com/eulerity/taskmanager/entity/Project.ja
           +va`                                                          
       320 +> - `src/main/java/com/eulerity/taskmanager/entity/Task.java`
       321 +>                                                            
       322 +> ## Verification                                            
       323 +> - `./mvnw -q compile` to confirm everything compiles.      
       324 +> - Start the app with `spring.jpa.show-sql=true` temporarily
           + to confirm Hibernate creates the `project` and `task` tables
           + with the expected columns, then revert any temporary propert
           +y change.

       380 +> # Guard against Jackson infinite recursion between Project 
           +and Task                                                     
       381 +>                                                            
       382 +> ## Context                                                 
       383 +> The user asked whether the bidirectional `Project.tasks` / 
           +`Task.project` relationship risks a circular-dependency infin
           +ite loop.                                                    
       384 +>                                                            
       385 +> **Analysis (no code needed to confirm this):**             
       386 +> - No circular *class* dependency — Java has no issue with t
           +wo classes mutually referencing each other.                  
       387 +> - No infinite loop during DB loading — both sides are `Fetc
           +hType.LAZY`, so Hibernate uses proxies instead of eagerly wal
           +king the full graph when loading a `Project` or `Task`.      
       388 +> - The one real risk: if a `Project` or `Task` entity were e
           +ver serialized directly to JSON by Jackson, it would recurse 
           +`Project → tasks → each Task → project → tasks → ...` and thr
           +ow a `StackOverflowError`. Since DTOs are the planned API con
           +tract, this shouldn't come up in normal use — but the user wa
           +nts a defensive guard added anyway.                          
       389 +>                                                            
       390 +> Also answered: getters/setters on `Project`/`Task` stay nec
           +essary even with DTOs in the picture. JPA annotations are pla
           +ced on fields, so Hibernate itself uses field access and does
           +n't require them — but the future service/mapping layer that 
           +will convert between entities and DTOs still needs a way to r
           +ead/write entity state, and idiomatic Java does that via gett
           +ers/setters (no Lombok in this project). No entity change nee
           +ded for this part.                                           
       391 +>                                                            
       392 +> ## Approach                                                
       393 +> Add `@JsonIgnore` (`com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonIg
           +nore`) to the `project` field on `Task` — the child side of t
           +he relationship. `spring-boot-starter-webmvc` already pulls i
           +n Jackson, so no new dependency is needed.                   
       394 +>                                                            
       395 +> ## Files to change                                         
       396 +> - `src/main/java/com/eulerity/taskmanager/entity/Task.java`

           +ield.

       417 +**Assistant:**                                               
       418 +> Good question — a few standard options, roughly from lighte
           +st to most robust:                                           
       419 +>                                                            
       420 +> **1. Environment variable placeholders (most common for thi
           +s)**                                                         
       421 +> Keep `application.properties` in git with a placeholder + l
           +ocal default:                                                
       422 +> ```                                                        
       423 +> spring.datasource.password=${DB_PASSWORD:password}         
       424 +> ```                                                        
       425 +> The real password (if it were ever sensitive) is set via an
           + actual env var (shell export, IDE run config, or CI secret) 
           +and never committed. The `:password` fallback still lets you 
           +run locally with zero setup.                                 
       426 +>                                                            
       427 +> **2. A gitignored profile-specific properties file**       
       428 +> Add `application-local.properties` (or `application-secrets
           +.properties`) to `.gitignore`, put real credentials there, an
           +d activate it with `spring.profiles.active=local`. Committed 
           +`application.properties` stays clean/generic. Your current `.
           +gitignore` (Spring Initializr default) doesn't exclude anythi
           +ng like this yet — you'd add the entry yourself.             
       429 +>                                                            
       430 +> **3. `.env` file + `spring.config.import`**                
       431 +> Spring Boot can import a `.env`-style file (`spring.config.
           +import=optional:file:.env[.properties]`) that you gitignore, 
           +similar spirit to option 2 but a single flat file instead of 
           +a profile.                                                   
       432 +>                                                            
       433 +> **4. Command-line / CI-injected args**                     
       434 +> Never put it in a file at all — pass `--spring.datasource.p
           +assword=...` at launch, or inject via your CI/CD secret store
           +. No local file risk, but less convenient for day-to-day `./m
           +vnw spring-boot:run`.                                        
       435 +>                                                            
       436 +> **5. A real secrets manager** (Vault, AWS/GCP Secrets Manag
           +er)                                                          
       437 +> Standard for production, overkill for local dev.           
       438 +>                                                            
       439 +> One thing worth weighing: this is the H2 **in-memory** cons
           +ole login — the "database" doesn't outlive the process, and `
           +admin`/`password` isn't protecting anything with real data be
           +hind it, so the actual risk of committing it is low compared 
           +to, say, a real Postgres password. Still fine to want the hab
           +it either way — happy to wire up whichever option you prefer 
           +(1 and 2 are the least friction for local dev).

       680 +> # Wire PUT /api/tasks/{id} to JPA                          
       681 +>                                                            
       682 +> ## Context                                                 
       683 +> `POST /api/tasks` and both `GET` endpoints are already wire
           +d to JPA. Now `PUT /api/tasks/{id}` needs to actually update 
           +a persisted `Task`, reusing `TaskRequestDto` and returning a 
           +status message like the create endpoint ("Task updated with i
           +d X"), with validation on both the id and the body, and a pro
           +per existence check.                                         
       684 +>                                                            
       685 +> ## Approach                                                
       686 +>                                                            
       687 +> ### Validation layers                                      
       688 +> - **id**: `@PathVariable Long id` — non-numeric → automatic
           + `400`.                                                      
       689 +> - **Body**: `@Valid @RequestBody TaskRequestDto request` — 
           +reuses existing constraints.                                 
       690 +> - **Existence check**: service looks up the task first; if 
           +absent, controller returns `404`.                            
       691 +> - **projectId validity**: same as create — invalid id throw
           +s `IllegalArgumentException`, mapped to `400`.               
       692 +>                                                            
       693 +> ### `service/TaskService.java` — add `updateTask(Long id, T
           +askRequestDto request)`                                      
       694 +> Returns `Optional<Task>` (empty = not found). When present,
           + updates `title`, `description`, `dueDate`, `priority`, `stat
           +us`. For `project`: a provided `projectId` resolves and sets 
           +the project; an omitted `projectId` **clears** the task's pro
           +ject association — standard full-replace `PUT` semantics.    
       695 +>                                                            
       696 +> ### `controller/TaskManagerController.java` — wire `updateT
           +ask`                                                         
       697 +> ```                                                        
       698 +> @PutMapping("/tasks/{id}")                                 
       699 +> public ResponseEntity<String> updateTask(@PathVariable Long
           + id, @Valid @RequestBody TaskRequestDto request) {           
       700 +>     try {                                                  
       701 +>         return taskService.updateTask(id, request)         
       702 +>                 .map(task -> ResponseEntity.ok("Task update
           +d with id " + task.getId()))                                 
       703 +>                 .orElseGet(() -> ResponseEntity.notFound().
           +build());                                                    
       704 +>     } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {                 
       705 +>         return ResponseEntity.badRequest().body(e.getMessag
           +e());                                                        
       706 +>     }                                                      
       707 +> }                                                          
       708 +> ```                                                        
       709 +> `200` on success, `404` if the id doesn't exist, `400` for 
           +validation failures or an invalid `projectId`.               
       710 +>                                                            
       711 +> ## Files to change                                         
       712 +> - `service/TaskService.java`, `controller/TaskManagerContro
           +ller.java`                                                   
       713 +>                                                            
       714 +> ## Verification                                            
       715 +> - `./mvnw -q compile`.                                     
       716 +> - `curl`: create, then full valid update (`200`), nonexiste
           +nt id (`404`), missing title (`400`), invalid `projectId` (`4
           +00`), and omitting `projectId` on a task that had one, then `
           +GET` it back to confirm `project` is now `null`.

       791 +**Assistant:**                                               
       792 +> For a project with no tasks, `project.getTasks()` returns a
           +n **empty `List<Task>`, never `null`** — the entity field is 
           +initialized as `new ArrayList<>()` (`entity/Project.java`), a
           +nd when Hibernate loads a `Project`, it backs that lazy `@One
           +ToMany` with a proxy collection that resolves to an empty lis
           +t (via `SELECT * FROM task WHERE project_id = ?` returning ze
           +ro rows) rather than `null`.                                 
       793 +>                                                            
       794 +> So in `ProjectService.toResponseDto()`:                    
       795 +> ```java                                                    
       796 +> dto.setTasks(project.getTasks().stream()                   
       797 +>         .map(this::toTaskSummaryDto)                       
       798 +>         .toList());                                        
       799 +> ```                                                        
       800 +> `.stream()` on an empty list just produces an empty stream,
           + `.map()` does nothing, `.toList()` returns an empty (but non
           +-null) list.                                                 
       801 +>                                                            
       802 +> You can see this in the earlier test output — "Minimal proj
           +ect" (id 2, no tasks created under it) came back as:         
       803 +> ```json                                                    
       804 +> {"description":null,"id":2,"name":"Minimal project","tasks"
           +:[]}                                                         
       805 +> ```                                                        
       806 +> `tasks` is `[]`, not `null` or a missing field.

       873 +## 24. Filtering, sorting, and pagination for `GET /api/tasks
           +`                                                            
       874 +                                                             
       875 +**User:**                                                    
       876 +> let's implement GET /tasks filtering using JpaSpecification
           +Executor and a TaskSpecification class. Support query params:
           + status (enum), priority (enum), dueBefore (LocalDate), dueAf
           +ter (LocalDate), projectId (Long). Sorting via sortBy (dueDat
           +e or priority) and sortDir (asc/desc, default asc). Paginatio
           +n via page (0-indexed) and size (default 20). Return a respon
           +se wrapper with content, page, size, totalElements, totalPage
           +s. All params optional and combinable.                       
       877 +                                                             
       878 +**Assistant (plan):**                                        
       879 +                                                             
       880 +> # Add filtering, sorting, and pagination to GET /api/tasks 
       881 +>                                                            
       882 +> ## Context                                                 
       883 +> `GET /api/tasks` currently returns every task with no way t
           +o narrow, order, or page results. As task volume grows this d
           +oesn't scale for the test UI or any future client. The user w
           +ants query-param-driven filtering (status, priority, due-date
           + range, project) built with Spring Data's `JpaSpecificationEx
           +ecutor` + a `TaskSpecification` class, plus sorting and pagin
           +ation, all optional and combinable, wrapped in a paged respon
           +se envelope.                                                 
       884 +>                                                            
       885 +> ## Approach                                                
       886 +>                                                            
       887 +> **`repository/TaskRepository.java`**                       
       888 +> Extend `JpaSpecificationExecutor<Task>` in addition to `Jpa
           +Repository<Task, Long>` to unlock `findAll(Specification<Task
           +>, Pageable)`.                                               
       889 +>                                                            
       890 +> **`specification/TaskSpecification.java`** (new package)   
       891 +> Static, null-argument-free factory methods, one per filter,
           + each returning a `Specification<Task>`:                     
       892 +> - `hasStatus(TaskStatus status)` → `cb.equal(root.get("stat
           +us"), status)`                                               
       893 +> - `hasPriority(TaskPriority priority)` → `cb.equal(root.get
           +("priority"), priority)`                                     
       894 +> - `dueBefore(LocalDate date)` → `cb.lessThanOrEqualTo(root.
           +get("dueDate"), date)`                                       
       895 +> - `dueAfter(LocalDate date)` → `cb.greaterThanOrEqualTo(roo
           +t.get("dueDate"), date)`                                     
       896 +> - `hasProjectId(Long projectId)` → `cb.equal(root.get("proj
           +ect").get("id"), projectId)`                                 
       897 +>                                                            
       898 +> Private constructor, no instance state — pure spec builder,
           + mirrors the DTO/entity file-per-class convention already use
           +d.                                                           
       899 +>                                                            
       900 +> **`dto/response/PagedResponseDto.java`** (new)             
       901 +> Generic wrapper: `content` (`List<T>`), `page`, `size`, `to
           +talElements` (`long`), `totalPages` (`int`), with getters/set
           +ters — same plain-POJO style as the other response DTOs.     
       902 +>                                                            
       903 +> **`service/TaskService.java`**                             
       904 +> Add `getFilteredTasks(TaskStatus status, TaskPriority prior
           +ity, LocalDate dueBefore, LocalDate dueAfter, Long projectId,
           + String sortBy, String sortDir, int page, int size)`:        
       905 +> 1. Build `Sort` — validate `sortBy` is exactly `"dueDate"` 
           +or `"priority"` (else throw `IllegalArgumentException`, match
           +ing the existing validation-error convention e.g. `resolvePro
           +ject`); `sortDir` `"desc"` (case-insensitive) → `DESC`, anyth
           +ing else → `ASC`.                                            
       906 +> 2. Build `Pageable` via `PageRequest.of(page, size, sort)` 
           +(invalid `page`/`size` naturally throw `IllegalArgumentExcept
           +ion` from Spring here — no extra checks needed).             
       907 +> 3. Build a combined `Specification<Task>` by collecting onl
           +y the non-null filters into a list and reducing with `Specifi
           +cation::and` (empty list → `null`, meaning "no restriction," 
           +which `findAll` accepts).                                    
       908 +> 4. Call `taskRepository.findAll(spec, pageable)`, map the r
           +eturned `Page<Task>` content through the existing `toResponse
           +Dto` mapper, and populate `PagedResponseDto` from `Page#getNu
           +mber/getSize/getTotalElements/getTotalPages`.                
       909 +>                                                            
       910 +> **`controller/TaskManagerController.java`**                
       911 +> Change `GET /tasks` to accept optional `@RequestParam`s: `s
           +tatus` (`TaskStatus`), `priority` (`TaskPriority`), `dueBefor
           +e`/`dueAfter` (`LocalDate`), `projectId` (`Long`), `sortBy` (
           +default `"dueDate"`), `sortDir` (default `"asc"`), `page` (de
           +fault `0`), `size` (default `20`). Delegate to `taskService.g
           +etFilteredTasks(...)`. Return type becomes `ResponseEntity<Ob
           +ject>` (mirrors the existing `createTask`/`updateTask` patter
           +n of catching `IllegalArgumentException` inline and returning
           + a `400` with the message) — success returns `PagedResponseDt
           +o<TaskResponseDto>`, failure returns the error string.       
       912 +>                                                            
       913 +> ## Files changed

      1034 +> # Global exception handling with a consistent error envelop
           +e                                                            
      1035 +>                                                            
      1036 +> ## Context                                                 
      1037 +> Error handling has been ad hoc so far. Today: bean-validati
           +on failures on `@Valid` bodies fall through to Spring's defau
           +lt error body; business-rule failures (`resolveProject`, `sor
           +tBy` validation, the update-time "status is required" check) 
           +are thrown as `IllegalArgumentException` and caught ad hoc pe
           +r-controller-method, returning a bare string; not-found cases
           + return `Optional`/`boolean` and the controller manually buil
           +ds an empty `404` with no body at all. The user wants exactly
           + two response categories — `400` for missing/invalid/malforme
           +d input (including unknown enum values) and `404` for referen
           +cing a resource that doesn't exist — both wrapped in `{error,
           + message, fields[]}`, built via a Spring `@RestControllerAdvi
           +ce` with per-exception-type handlers and one generic fallback
           +.                                                            
      1038 +>                                                            
      1039 +> ## Approach                                                
      1040 +>                                                            
      1041 +> **`dto/response/ErrorResponseDto.java`** (new) — `error`, `
           +message`, `fields` (`List<FieldErrorDto>`).                  
      1042 +>                                                            
      1043 +> **`dto/response/FieldErrorDto.java`** (new) — `field`, `mes
           +sage`.                                                       
      1044 +>                                                            
      1045 +> **`exception/ResourceNotFoundException.java`** (new package
           +) — simple `RuntimeException` subclass with a `String message
           +` constructor.                                               
      1046 +>                                                            
      1047 +> **`exception/GlobalExceptionHandler.java`** (new) — `@RestC
           +ontrollerAdvice` with handlers, most specific first, generic 
           +`Exception` last:                                            
      1048 +> - `ResourceNotFoundException` → `404`, `error="RESOURCE_NOT
           +_FOUND"`.                                                    
      1049 +> - `MethodArgumentNotValidException` (bean-validation) → `40
           +0`, `error="VALIDATION_FAILED"`, `message="One or more fields
           + are invalid"`, `fields` from `ex.getBindingResult().getField
           +Errors()`.                                                   
      1050 +> - `HttpMessageNotReadableException` (malformed JSON / unkno
           +wn enum literal) → `400`; unwrap a Jackson `InvalidFormatExce
           +ption` cause to report the specific `field`, else a generic "
           +Malformed JSON request" message.                             
      1051 +> - `MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException` (bad `@PathVariable
           +`/`@RequestParam`) → `400`, one `fields` entry naming the par
           +ameter.                                                      
      1052 +> - `IllegalArgumentException` (existing business-rule checks
           +) → `400`, `error="VALIDATION_FAILED"`, `message=ex.getMessag
           +e()`, `fields=[]`.                                           
      1053 +> - `Exception` (generic fallback) → `500`, `error="INTERNAL_
           +ERROR"`.                                                     
      1054 +>
